```{r}
#| label: setup
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(here)
# quarto renders from docs/, where here() would root (it has _quarto.yml); i_am() pins the
# root to the repo, so this runs the same under quarto and line by line.
i_am("docs/ais_trail.qmd")
source(here("R/paths.R"))

# The trail is a parquet dataset partitioned by year and month; these are only shortcuts for
# `open_dataset() |> filter()`, which is all an analyst needs.
trail <- function(years, vids = NULL) {
  d <- duckdbfs::open_dataset(fd_curated("ais", "trail")) |> filter(year %in% !!years)
  if (!is.null(vids)) d <- d |> filter(vid %in% !!vids)
  d
}
trail_match <- function(years, vids = NULL) {
  d <- duckdbfs::open_dataset(fd_curated("ais", "trail_match")) |> filter(year %in% !!years)
  if (!is.null(vids)) d <- d |> filter(vid %in% !!vids)
  d
}
```

## What it is

`curated/ais/trail` has one row per fix (the AIS pings and the onboard GPS logger fixes of every
vessel) with the AIS voyage, the logbook station and the logbook trip it belongs to. It is a parquet
dataset partitioned by year and month, so there is nothing to call: open it and work on it in dplyr.
Rules and numbers are in plan 010 (`curate/plans/010-ping-activity-link.md`, §3 and §11) and plan 011
(Phase 5); `curated/ais/trail_match` holds every (fix, station) match.

```r
trail <- duckdbfs::open_dataset(fd_curated("ais", "trail"))
trail |> filter(year == 2019, vid == 1277) |> collect()          # one vessel-year
trail |> filter(year == 2019, month == 6) |> count(gear_class)    # a month
duckdbfs::open_dataset(fd_curated("ais", "trail_match"))          # one row per (fix, station)
```

Whacky points, positions no vessel could have reached, are not in the trail. `curate/ais_ping_clean.R`
removes them before voyages, stays, distances or speeds are worked out: first placeholder positions, where
the longitude equals the latitude, (0, 0) included (`curate/corrections/ais_invalid_position.yml`), then
the rest with `ramb::whack_clean()`. They are about 0.5 % of all pings, and they are kept in
`staging/ais/ping_whacky`, where `whack_stage` says which test flagged each one (decision 067).

The columns added to the pings (the voyage columns come from the AIS voyage, the station columns from the logbook stations):

| column | meaning |
|---|---|
| `stay_pid`, `trip` | harbour of the stay the fix is in (NA at sea); the AIS voyage number within `vid` and `year` |
| `.tid_voyage`, `schema_voyage`, `n_tid_voyage` | the logbook trip of the voyage — filled only when exactly one trip is on it; `n_tid_voyage` counts them (0 = none) |
| n_sid | number of station windows that contain the fix (0 = none) |
| `.sid`, `schema`, `.tid` | the station and trip — filled **only** when `n_sid == 1` |
| `gear`, `gear_class`, `target`, `target2` | gear of the station (ICES code, class), its ICES target assemblage (`target`, e.g. `CRU`) and the finer Icelandic target (`target2`, e.g. `NEP`); NA for adb stations, which carry no gear code |
| `s1`, `s2` | the speed range (knots) of the gear class that `fishing` is tested against; NA for a gear with no range |
| `phase`, `phase_frac` | `tow`, `haul`, `set`, `jig` or `day`; how far through the window the fix is (0–1) |
| `win_basis` | how the window was drawn (`recorded`, `derived`, `capped`, ...) |
| `fishing` | inside a tow/haul/jig/day window **and** speed inside that gear's `[s1, s2]` |

Ambiguity stays ambiguous: there is no "primary" station. A station is the pair `(.sid, schema)`,
never `.sid` alone. (Bare `sid` is the species code.)

## Following a whole trip

A trip is `(.tid, schema)`. The helper below takes one, reads its station windows, and returns the
fixes from three hours before the trip's first window to three hours after its last. The windows
returned are **every window of the vessel that overlaps that span**, not only the trip's own: a
neighbouring trip's tow or a `day` window can claim the fixes at the edges, and the check has to
know about them. (A fix outside every window has no `.tid`, but it may carry `.tid_voyage`; here the span margin stands in for the voyage.)

```{r}
#| label: helpers
trip_trail <- function(tid, schema, margin_h = 3) {
  swall <- duckdbfs::open_dataset(fd_curated("logbook", "station_window.parquet"))
  own <- swall |> filter(.tid == !!tid, schema == !!schema) |> collect()
  vid <- unique(own$vid)
  lo <- min(own$w_start) - margin_h * 3600
  hi <- max(own$w_end) + margin_h * 3600
  yrs <- unique(as.integer(format(c(lo, hi), "%Y")))
  sw <- swall |> filter(vid == !!vid) |> collect() |>
    filter(w_end >= lo, w_start <= hi) |> arrange(w_start)
  tr <- trail(yrs, vid) |> filter(time >= !!lo, time <= !!hi) |> collect()
  list(vid = vid, tid = tid, own = own, sw = sw, tr = tr)
}

# The check: plain R, not the join. A fix belongs to the tow-type windows holding its time, and
# only when there is none does a `day` window claim it (the tier rule in R/trail_sql.R).
prove <- function(x) {
  sw <- x$sw; tr <- x$tr
  k <- lapply(tr$time, function(t) {
    h <- which(t >= sw$w_start & t <= sw$w_end)
    h1 <- h[sw$phase[h] != "day"]
    if (length(h1)) h1 else h
  })
  stopifnot(identical(as.integer(tr$n_sid), lengths(k)))
  sid <- vapply(k, function(h) if (length(h) == 1) sw$.sid[h] else NA_real_, numeric(1))
  stopifnot(identical(as.numeric(tr$.sid), sid))
  # fishing: a non-set window among the claimants whose own [s1, s2] holds the speed; NA when no speed
  # and some claimant could have made it fishing; FALSE in no window
  fish <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(tr)), function(i) {
    h <- k[[i]]
    if (is.na(tr$speed[i])) {
      if (any(sw$phase[h] != "set" & !is.na(sw$s1[h]))) NA else FALSE
    } else {
      any(sw$phase[h] != "set" & tr$speed[i] >= sw$s1[h] & tr$speed[i] <= sw$s2[h], na.rm = TRUE)
    }
  }, logical(1))
  stopifnot(identical(tr$fishing, fish))
  stopifnot(!any(tr$fishing & tr$n_sid == 0, na.rm = TRUE), !anyNA(tr$fishing[tr$n_sid == 0]))
  tibble(fixes = nrow(tr), in_a_window = sum(tr$n_sid > 0), ambiguous = sum(tr$n_sid > 1),
         fishing = sum(tr$fishing, na.rm = TRUE), no_speed = sum(is.na(tr$fishing)), mismatches = 0L)
}

plot_speed <- function(x) {
  ggplot(x$tr, aes(time, speed)) +
    geom_rect(data = filter(x$sw, phase != "day"),
              aes(xmin = w_start, xmax = w_end, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.2) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = unique(c(x$own$s1, x$own$s2)), linetype = 3) +
    geom_line(colour = "grey60") +
    geom_point(aes(colour = fishing, shape = provider), size = 1.8) +
    labs(y = "speed (kn)")
}

per_station <- function(x) {
  x$tr |>
    filter(n_sid == 1) |>
    group_by(.sid, phase) |>
    summarise(fixes = n(), gps = sum(provider == "gps"), fishing = sum(fishing, na.rm = TRUE),
              median_speed = median(speed, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    left_join(x$sw |> select(.sid, s1, s2), by = ".sid")
}
```

`prove()` stops the page if a single fix disagrees on `n_sid`, `.sid` or `fishing`, so a clean
render is the evidence.

## Example 1: a slow trawler with a sparse logger

Vessel 1787, trip `-1018639`: six recorded bottom-trawl tows on 2019-01-04.

```{r}
#| label: trip1
x1 <- trip_trail("-1018639", "afli")
x1$sw |> transmute(.sid, .tid, gear, phase, w_start, w_end, win_basis, s1, s2)
x1$tr |> count(provider, name = "fixes")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-speed1
#| fig-cap: "Vessel 1787, trip -1018639. Shaded bands are the tow windows; colour is `fishing`, shape is the provider."
#| fig-height: 3.5
plot_speed(x1)
```

```{r}
#| label: prove1
prove(x1)
per_station(x1)
```

The logger gives this vessel only three fixes (it has about 2,900 for the whole of 2019; most
vessels have a fix every 5–10 minutes). Also, `fishing` is stricter than "in a tow window": it
needs the speed inside the gear's `[s1, s2]`, and 1787 is a slow trawler (plan 010 §11: 1.9–2.4 kn
in tows) below the OTB lower limit of 2.62 kn. Use `n_sid == 1` for "belongs to a station" and
`fishing` for "was towing at fishing speed".

## Example 2: a typical trawler, logger and AIS together

Vessel 2894, trip `-1020724`: four recorded tows on 2019-01-17, trawling at about 3.7 kn, with a
5-minute logger.

```{r}
#| label: trip2
x2 <- trip_trail("-1020724", "afli")
x2$sw |> transmute(.sid, .tid, gear, phase, w_start, w_end, win_basis, s1, s2)
x2$tr |> count(provider, name = "fixes")
```

The span reaches back to 23:00 on the 16th, so two windows that are **not** this trip's are in
the table: the tow of the previous trip that began at 22:22, and a `day` window covering the whole
16th (synthesised, because that station had no usable time). The `day` window takes the fixes
after that tow ends, as the tier rule says, and `prove()` knows it.

```{r}
#| label: fig-speed2
#| fig-cap: "Vessel 2894, trip -1020724."
#| fig-height: 3.5
plot_speed(x2)
```

```{r}
#| label: prove2
prove(x2)
per_station(x2)
```

## When a fix belongs to more than one station

Where two windows overlap, `n_sid > 1` and `.sid` is left empty. The unambiguous alternative is
`trail_match`, which has one row per (fix, station) so the analyst decides:

```{r}
#| label: long
trail_match(2019, x1$vid) |>
  filter(time >= !!min(x1$tr$time), time <= !!max(x1$tr$time)) |>
  count(.sid, phase, win_basis) |>
  collect() -> long_n
long_n
stopifnot(sum(long_n$n) == sum(x1$tr$n_sid))   # one row per (fix, station)
```

For this trip no fix is ambiguous. To see how common it is over a whole vessel-year:

```{r}
#| label: ambiguity
trail(2019, x1$vid) |>
  count(n_sid, name = "fixes") |>
  collect() |>
  arrange(n_sid)
```

## Where the numbers come from

- `curated/ais/trail`, `trail_match` — built from `ping_trail`, `station_window` and `link/trip_voyage` by `curate/ais_trail.R`; checks `curated/check/trail_agreement` (the station and the voyage name the same trip in 99.6 % of fixes that have both) and `trail_sid_coverage`.
- `curated/ais/ping_trail/year=*` — AIS (stk, astd, astdB, emodnet) and the GPS logger, unique on `(vid, time)`, speed in knots.
- `curated/logbook/station_window.parquet` — one row per station window, with `win_basis` saying how it was drawn.
- This page and the code behind it were written with AI assistance (Claude); the checks above, not the code's say-so, establish the result.
